answer: Tie each agent to one mailbox on a domain two years old. First, the network mails a signed challenge there. Second, the agent answers in 24 hours with a DKIM-signed reply to prove control, and one mailbox backs one identity, a small knoll in an open field. Third, a caught sybil blacklists its domain for a year, so one ripple of fraud taints its siblings. Fourth, identities re-verify yearly or go quiet. Buying 1,000 aged domains costs about 200,000 dollars, plus 60 dollars a year per mailbox. Like a jade seal pressed into wax, it leaves a mark cheap to check and costly to forge in bulk.
